jobs.title: PHNIX Health Program Manager
jobs.description:
Job Summary

#CA-SS

This position has state-wide visibility and responsibilities. The incumbent works directly with the California Department of Public Health’s (CDPH) Director and state Lead Epidemiologist and will closely coordinate Public Health Network Information Exchange (PHNIX) project activities in collaboration with the Chief Deputy Directors and other senior executive level administrators across CDPH. The incumbent will interact with state organizations, industry, healthcare and community leaders, as well as private foundation officers and trustees, industry representatives, researchers and others in carrying out the broad responsibilities of this position in relation to the PHNIX project. Must understand government administration and how projects which may cross a wide variety of fields can be implemented and be able to express these concepts in a compelling way to statewide stakeholders, business partners, officers and trustees.

Reports directly to the State Epidemiologist providing direction and leadership on statewide epidemiology and technology projects, including serving as lead liaison between PHNIX Institute and CDPH. Coordinates with the Chief Data Strategist, Chief Information Officer, modeling and informatics team and other critical areas to ensure that work of the PHNIX project is in alignment with other department efforts.

Apply By Date September 9, 2026 at 11:59PM;
Interviews and recruiting process may occur at any time.

Minimum Qualifications - For full consideration, applicants are encouraged to upload license and/or certification if required of the position

Bachelor's degree in Business Studies, Economics, Sciences, or another similar analytical degree and/or equivalent experience/training.
At least five (5) years of leadership-level work in federal, state, or local government.
At least five (5) years of experience developing collaborative multidisciplinary working relationships and social networks central to innovation and the promotion of scientific discovery.
Extensive experience within large organizations and/or foundations, successfully cultivating strategic partnerships, leading cross-functional teams, and driving innovative solutions through the execution of complex initiatives, transformative business concepts, and organizational best practices.
Broad organizational skills in developing, authoring, and launching business initiatives for large strategic projects.
Demonstrated ability to identify, understand, analyze, and interpret complex written material, business contracts and financial data and effectively synthesize and communicate results of analyses.
Demonstrated strategic and critical thinking to executives from within and outside a large public or government organization, and skills to think strategically and serve as a sounding board for executive managers.
Demonstrated knowledge and skills to clearly describe systems and programs to potential partners and investors.
Excellent verbal and written communication, presentation, and public speaking skills.
Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office software and database applications (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Access).

Preferred Qualifications

Degree in information technology, informatics or course work in epidemiology or related field.
An advanced educational qualification, Ph.D, JD, Graduate Business Degree (e.g., Masters of Business or Public Administration) or equivalent combination of education and experience is preferred.
Experience in academic health and technology settings and community engagement.
Experience in Public Health.
Experience in public communications and media.
Ability to interact diplomatically with diverse personalities and to exercise judgment and tact in interactions with faculty, staff, students and the public.
Ability to exercise initiative, originality, and judgement in applying established principles and practices to new and innovative opportunities.
Ability to represent the University at the highest levels and in public forums with professionalism and integrity.
Proven strong political acumen skills and ability to apply in diverse, complex organization.
Proven ability to apply high ethical standards to business practices and decision-making.
Proven ability to handle highly sensitive and confidential issues that require independent judgement and strict discretion, and maintain strict confidentiality of sensitive, confidential and/or privileged information.
Ability to represent the University at the highest levels and in public forums with professionalism and integrity.

Key Responsibilities

50% - Strategic Partnerships
25% - Innovation Strategy
25% - Facilitation of Leadership

Department Overview

The core activities of the CDPH are protecting and improving the health of all Californians through a wide range of public health activities, including disease prevention, health promotion, emergency preparedness, environmental health, food safety, and health equity initiatives. The Department of Public Health Sciences is a large, complex teaching, research, and clinical department in the UC Davis School of Medicine. The mission of the Department of Public Health Sciences is to improve the health of people using approaches based in epidemiology, biostatistics, economics, and behavioral science through research, educational programs, clinical programs, public service, and policy development.

The Public Health Network Information Exchange (PHNIX), a California-led Initiative Under The California Department Of Public Health (CDPH), Was Created To Modernize Public Health Infrastructure And Protect Science-driven Decision-making. Its Core Mission Statement And Focus Revolve Around Building a More Resilient Public Health Network Through Three Strategic Pillars

Innovation: Developing advanced technologies and data infrastructures. The PHNIX Innovation Institute was established to develop, validate, and scale public-benefit health technologies that improve outcomes and lower costs.
Collaboration: Strengthening networks across regional, national and global partners, including cross-sector collaborations. This aims to align strategies and fill gaps left by shifting federal policies.
Communication: Engaging communities and empowering the public to make informed, healthy decisions by providing clear, trustworthy information.

POSITION INFORMATION

Salary or Pay Range: $10,466.67 - $22,333.33
Salary Frequency: Monthly
Annual Salary: $125,600.00 - $268,000.00; budgeted up to $218,000/annually
Salary Grade: Grade 27

jobs.title: Petco Love - Data Analyst
jobs.description:
Want to help pets live their best lives?

We’re proud to be where the pets go and where the pet people go. If you want to make a real difference, create an exciting career path, feel welcome to be your whole self and nurture your wellbeing, Petco is the place for you
.

Our core values capture that spirit as we work to improve lives by doing what’s right for pets and people.

Pet First – Protect & Empower. All pets should Live their Best Life. We put the needs of pets and pet parents at the center of everything we do.
Foster the Fun – Connect & Bond. Our Passion for pets brings us together! We celebrate the journey of pet parenthood through district experiences, products, and services.
Let’s Go! Own & Commit. We are stronger as One Petco team. We bring our unique superpowers and champion authenticity in everyone to drive success.

About Petco

We’re proud to be "where the pets go"
to find everything they need to live their best lives for more than 60 years — from their favorite meals and toys, to trusted supplies and expert support from people who get it, because we live it. We believe in the universal truths of pet parenthood — the boundless boops, missing slippers, late night zoomies and everything in between. And we’re here for it. Every tail wag, every vet visit, every step of the way. We are 29,000+
strong and together we nurture the pet-human bond in more than 1,500
Petco stores across the U.S., Mexico and Puerto Rico, 250+
Vetco Total Care hospitals, hundreds of preventive care clinics and eight distribution centers. In 1999, we founded Petco Love. Together, we support thousands of local animal welfare groups nationwide and have helped find homes for approximately 7 million animals
through in-store adoption events.

About Petco Love

Petco Love is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit on a mission to create a future where no pet is ever lost, separated, or without a loving home. Our flagship platform, Petco Love Lost, is an AI/ML-powered national lost and found pet search tool that has facilitated over 120,000 reunions annually, covers 90% of U.S. animal shelters, and serves millions of pet parents across the country.

We operate at the intersection of technology, animal welfare, and community impact. Our small, mission-driven team moves fast, works closely with partners across the shelter and rescue ecosystem, and builds products that matter.

The Role

We are looking for a Data Analyst to join Petco Love's product and marketing team. This is a hands-on role with high visibility across our platform, GTM initiatives, and partner integrations. You will own our analytics infrastructure end-to-end, from raw event tracking in GA4 through BigQuery to dashboards and decision-ready insights that directly inform product and marketing strategy.

You will work closely with the Chief Product Officer, CTO, and Customer Success team. You do not need to be a data scientist, but you need to be deeply curious, self-directed, and excited about using data to drive mission impact.

Essential Job Functions

Analytics & Data Infrastructure

Own and maintain our GA4 implementation, including event schema design, custom dimensions, conversion tracking, and data layer governance across petcolovelost.org and related product surfaces.
Build and manage our GA4 to BigQuery pipeline as our primary analytics data warehouse; design schemas, write transformation queries, and maintain data quality standards.
Develop and maintain dashboards and reports that track product performance, user behavior, funnel conversion, and mission KPIs (reunions, sign-ups, NPS, shelter engagement).
Apply advanced analytical techniques including behavioral segmentation, funnel analysis, predictive modeling, and cohort analysis to surface insights across the pet owner and shelter user journey.
Mine large datasets to identify patterns in user behavior, feature engagement, search performance, and platform outcomes to inform product roadmap and marketing decisions.

GTM Strategy & Marketing Analytics

Partner with the product and marketing team to design and analyze GTM experiments including A/B tests, flow variants, and audience segmentation strategies across email, SMS, and in-product channels.
Build and maintain audience models and signal-based segmentation to power our product and marketing automation architecture, including found-pet, lost-pet, and partner-specific flows.
Provide data support for partnership GTM initiatives including revenue modeling, audience sizing, and performance tracking.
Translate campaign and flow performance data (open rates, click rates, conversions, reunion outcomes) into clear recommendations that optimize acquisition, engagement, and lifetime value.
Build accurate financial projections and impact forecasts based on deep behavioral analysis to support board reporting, partner proposals, and strategic planning.

Animal Welfare & Mission Insights

Apply understanding of animal welfare industry dynamics to contextualize data findings and surface insights specific to shelter intake, outcomes, lost and found behavior, and pet owner decision-making.
Analyze survey and behavioral research data to identify unmet needs and product opportunities.
Validate AI/ML model outputs and surface quality signals from our facial recognition matching and pet identity systems to help the engineering team maintain accuracy and reduce false positives.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

Collaborate with Customer Success to identify trends in user-reported issues, NPS driver analysis, and segment-level satisfaction signals.
Present findings to senior leadership and board stakeholders; translate complex analysis into clear narrative, actionable recommendations, and visual summaries that drive decisions.
Contribute to long-term projects from scoping through execution, partnering with engineering, design, and external platform teams (shelters, rescue partners, plaform integrations).

Required Skills And Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in economics, statistics, math, computer science, or related field; Master's preferred.
1-2+ years of experience in a data analytics or quantitative role.
Hands-on experience with GA4 — event tracking, custom dimensions, exploration reports, and integration with BigQuery (Google Analytics 4 to BigQuery export).
Strong SQL skills; experience querying large, complex datasets across multiple sources.
Experience with statistical programming languages (Python preferred; R or SAS acceptable).
Demonstrated ability to build clear, decision-oriented dashboards and visualizations (Looker, Tableau, Google Data Studio, or similar).
Exceptional communication skills — ability to translate complex data into plain, compelling narratives for non-technical stakeholders including executives and board members.
Ability to prioritize and manage multiple workstreams simultaneously in a fast-moving environment.
Genuine intellectual curiosity and commitment to solving hard problems with limited resources.

Nice to Have

Experience with Klaviyo or similar marketing automation platforms — audience segmentation, flow analytics, or A/B testing.
Familiarity with animal welfare, pet tech, nonprofit, or mission-driven organizations.
Experience with AI/ML data validation or working alongside data science teams on model quality.
Knowledge of the shelter/rescue ecosystem, pet reunification, or pet adoption platforms.

jobs.title: Clinical Program Manager
jobs.description:
At Gilead, we’re creating a healthier world for all people. For more than 35 years, we’ve tackled diseases such as HIV, viral hepatitis, COVID-19 and cancer – working relentlessly to develop therapies that help improve lives and to ensure access to these therapies across the globe. We continue to fight against the world’s biggest health challenges, and our mission requires collaboration, determination and a relentless drive to make a difference.

Every member of Gilead’s team plays a critical role in the discovery and development of life-changing scientific innovations. Our employees are our greatest asset as we work to achieve our bold ambitions, and we’re looking for the next wave of passionate and ambitious people ready to make a direct impact.

We believe every employee deserves a great leader. People Leaders are the cornerstone to the employee experience at Gilead and Kite. As a people leader now or in the future, you are the key driver in evolving our culture and creating an environment where every employee feels included, developed and empowered to fulfil their aspirations. Join Gilead and help create possible, together.

Job Description

The Clinical Program Manager
is responsible for the worldwide execution of all Phase I - IV clinical trials across all Gilead therapeutic areas. Clinical Operations plays a key role in ensuring all Gilead clinical trials are performed in accordance with applicable SOPs, company policies and regulatory guidelines to provide timely and high-quality clinical data that supports global registration and commercialization of Gilead’s products.

You will oversee and be responsible for the successful execution of studies and/or multiple studies within a program or multiple programs, including financial responsibility. You will be responsible for the resource management of studies, including ongoing assessment of resource needs and optimal deployment of resources to support a fluid ‘One Ops’ workforce.

You will participate and engage in Clinical Operations and/or cross-functional organizational change initiatives. You may act as the business process owner (BPO) and/or serve as a subject matter expert for Clinical Operations processes. You will encourage an innovative mindset by championing new ideas and initiatives and incorporating best practices, external benchmarking, and standardization across Clinical Operations.

This is a Hybrid position, 3 days on-site (Tues -Thurs). Will not consider fully remote candidates.

jobs.title: Care Manager II - Case Management
jobs.description:
Description

Summary:

The Care Manager (CM) II works in collaboration with the patient/family, physicians and multidisciplinary team members to ensure patient progression through the continuum of care and to develop a plan of care for each assigned patient from admission through discharge. The CM is responsible for identifying, initiating and managing optimal patient flow/throughput to enhance continuity of care, smooth and safe transitions, patient satisfaction, patient safety, and length of stay management. Support and expertise are provided through comprehensive assessment, planning, implementation, and overall evaluation of individual patient needs. Care Coordination and Discharge Planning are both responsibilities of this role. The CM assesses and responds to patient/family needs by coordinating efforts of other team members and identifies and resolves barriers that hinder effective patient care. The CM adheres to departmental and organizational goals, objectives, standards of performance, policies and procedures, and continually assures regulatory compliance.

Responsibilities

Meets expectations of the applicable OneCHRISTUS Competencies: Leader of Self, Leader of Others, or Leader of Leaders.
Coordinates the integration of case management functions into the patient care and discharge planning processes in collaboration with other hospital departments, external service organizations, agencies, and healthcare facilities.
Coordinates/facilitates patient care progression throughout the continuum of care in an efficient and cost-effective manner.
Serves as resource, provides support, and advocates on behalf of the patient related to treatment decisions and end of life issues.
Closely monitor patient length of stay in regard to the geometric mean length of stay and communicate/collaborate with appropriate interdisciplinary team members to remove barriers and expedite discharge.
Implements and monitors the patient’s plan of care to ensure effectiveness and appropriateness of services.
Identifies and escalates local and system barriers that are impeding diagnostic or treatment progress and issues related to quality and risk as appropriate in a timely manner.
Proactively identifies and resolves delays and obstacles to discharge.
Uses advanced conflict resolution skills as necessary to ensure timely resolution of issues.
Collaborates with medical staff, nursing staff, and ancillary staff to eliminate barriers to efficient delivery of care in the appropriate setting.
Interviews patients/families to obtain information about social, emotional, and financial factors which impact health status to develop comprehensive discharge planning assessment and care plan.
Assesses needs for discharge planning and continuing care/resource support following discharge; independently makes recommendations to patients and families regarding post-acute level of care needs and options including:
Acute Rehabilitation Placement
Nursing Home or Skilled Nursing placement
Psychiatric or Substance Abuse placement
New Dialysis
Child/Adult/Domestic Abuse
Home Health/Hospice Referrals
Legal issues (adoptions, guardianship)
Assistance with Advance Directives
Community Resource needs
Financial Issues/Funding options
DME Referrals and Coordination
Social Determinants of Health

Initiates discharge planning at the time of admission and makes post-hospital service referrals based upon information gathered during assessment and interactions with physicians, multidisciplinary care team, and payors as indicated.
Acts as patient advocate by negotiating for, and coordinating, resources with payors, agencies, and vendors.
Ensures that all elements critical to the plan of care have been communicated to the patient/family and members of the healthcare team and are documented as necessary to assure continuity of care.
Provide appropriate interventions which demonstrate knowledge of and sensitivity toward cultural diversity and the religious, developmental, health literacy, and educational backgrounds of the patient population.
Assesses the patient’s formal and informal support system as well as available benefits and/or community resources.
Meets directly with patient/family to assess needs and develop and individualized care plan in collaboration with the physician.
Ensures and maintains plan consensus from patient/family, physician and payor.
Provides education, information, direction, and support related to patient’s goals of care.
Acts as patient advocate to develop treatment plan and coordinate patient care and to transition patient to the appropriate next level of care.
Demonstrates and promotes respect for the dignity and rights of every patient while adhering to the safety standards and practices of the organization and the nursing profession.
Collaborates with the physician and other health care professionals to promote appropriate use of medical center resources.
Provides information and support to patients and families, helping them access needed resources within the medical center and community.
Actively participates in clinical performance improvement activities involving length of stay, resource utilization, avoidable days, cost per case, and readmissions.
Measures effectiveness of interventions through direct communication with post-acute care providers, patients, and caregivers.
Promotes individual professional growth and development by meeting requirements for mandatory/continuing education and skills competency.
Actively participates in Multidisciplinary/Patient Care Progression Rounds.
Escalates cases as appropriate and per policy to Physician Advisors and/or CM Director.
Documents in the medical record per regulatory and department guidelines.
May be asked to assist with special projects.
May serve a preceptor or orienter to new associates.
Assumes responsibility for professional growth and development.
Must have excellent verbal and written communication and ability to interact with diverse populations.
Must have critical and analytical thinking skills.
Must have demonstrated clinical competency.
Must have the ability to Multitask and to function in a stressful and fast paced environment.
Must have working knowledge of discharge planning, utilization management, case management, performance improvement, and managed care reimbursement.
Must have understanding of pre-acute and post-acute levels of care and community resources.
Must have ability to work independently and exercise sound judgment in interactions with physicians, payors, patients and their families.
Must be understanding of internal and external resources and knowledge of available community resources.
Must have the ability to move around the hospital to all areas for the majority of the workday while in office the rest of the day; general office and hospital environment.

Education/Skills

Job Requirements:

Graduate of an accredited school of nursing (BSN preferred) or Masters Degree in Social Work (MSW) required or demonstrated success in CHRISTUS Care Manager I Position for at least 5 years on top of the required experience in lieu of education required.

Experience

Two or more years clinical experience with one year in the acute care setting preferred.

Licenses, Registrations, or Certifications

RN or LMSW in the state of employment is required for new hires.
LBSW accepted for associates with 5+ years of demonstrated success and experience in CHRISTUS Care Manager I role.
Certification in Case Management preferred.
BLS preferred.

The work you do here impacts the lives of millions of people for the better. Come build the health care system of tomorrow, making it more responsive, affordable, and equitable. This position will be the primary care manager for members with complex medical or behavioral needs who aren't otherwise managed by the team's clinicians. The CHW works assertively to locate and engage members in the community. They will develop individualized plans of care that focus on the member's definition of success. The CHW identifies and overcome barriers to goal achievement, including SDOH barriers. This position will work in collaboration with the interdisciplinary clinical care management team (Pod) to advance interventions aligned with a member's readiness to change. CHWs will approach their member work with an understanding of how inequities drive health disparities. CHWs will promote health equity.

Working Schedule:
Schedule is Monday through Friday between the hours of 8 am to 5 pm. This position is a field-based position with a home-based office. You will work from home when not in the field.

Locations will vary but within the following counties of Florida:
Alachua, Bradford, Citrus, Miami Dade, Monroe, Columbia, Dixie, Gilchrist, Hamilton, Hernando, Lafayette, Lake, Levy, Marion, Putnam, Sumter, Suwannee, Union, Baker, Clay, Duval, Flager, Nassau, St Johns and Volusia.

Local travel up to 10% and mileage is reimbursed at current government rate.

Locate and engage members in the community

Assist member in development of personal wellness plan / health crisis plan

Preferred Qualifications

Bachelor's Degree (or higher) in Social Work or related subject
LPN (Licensed Practical Nurse) Licensure or CNA / HHA
Bilingual in [Spanish]
Community Health Worker (CHW) Accreditation
Experience working in team-based care
Experience working in Managed Care
Lived experience (self or family) in managing or overcoming a chronic health, behavioral health or substance use condition
Telephonic case management experience or customer service
Demonstrated knowledge of Medicare and Medicaid benefits

Soft Skills

Possess a strong work ethic
Ability to listen skillfully, collect relevant information, build rapport and respond to customers in a compassionate manner
Ability to adapt to change in the workplace
Ability to work independently and as a part of a team
Ability to interact with internal and external customers in a corporate environment
Must possess a positive and motivated attitude
Willingness to adapt to multiple external environments and settings

Ability to transition from office to field locations multiple times a day
Must possess transportation to visit clients in various locations
Ability to travel varied distances and multiple terrains to visit assigned client locations
Ability to carry equipment to and from field locations needed for face to face member visits (ex. laptop, stethoscope, blood pressure cuff, etc.)

We’re building a world of health around every individual — shaping a more connected, convenient and compassionate health experience. At CVS Health®, you’ll be surrounded by passionate colleagues who care deeply, innovate with purpose, hold ourselves accountable and prioritize safety and quality in everything we do. Join us and be part of something bigger – helping to simplify health care one person, one family and one community at a time.

Title:
Community Health Worker

Company:
Oak Street Health

Role Description

The purpose of a Community Health Worker (CHW) at Oak Street Health is to act as the bridge between our patients, community, and medical systems in order to remove barriers and increase wellness across all life domains. A CHW is a patient’s advocate or liaison, accompanying patients through proactive in-person and phone outreach based on their care needs to promote health literacy and increase access to resources needed to live healthier lives. High levels of flexibility, problem solving, strong communication, and an intimate knowledge of the community served are required to be successful.

CHWs work closely with Medical Social Workers to manage patient care plans, support care team decision making, and coordinate clinical and complementary services needed to provide high quality health care and improve the quality and cultural competence of service delivery. CHWs are expected to work within their scope of practice. There is no expected clinical license for this position.

Core Responsibilities

Establish and maintain strong interpersonal relationships with patients, community organizations, team members, and partners to coordinate patient needs
Manage patient referrals defined by the care team & collaborate with the Medical Social Worker on action plan
Facilitate communication between all identified parties involved in patients’ care as needed (e.g., family members, caregivers, medical providers, community-based organizations)
Form relationships with and build an inventory of local community organizations that may benefit our patients
Connect patients to state and local community resources related to housing, transportation, food, and activities of daily living among other social and physical barriers to health.
Assist patients with completion of applications for accessing eligible benefits and resources
Promote goal setting and achievement to improve patients’ quality of life and self efficacy with patients. Goal definitions are agreed upon by the care team
Meet with patients in patient-centered and patient-preferred locations (e.g., Oak Street Health center, patient’s home, external medical provider facility, community setting)
Community Health Workers should plan to spend about half of their time outside of the center in patient-centered locations; this means having access to a reliable means of transportation to do so is required
Drive engagement with high risk individuals (e.g., completed specialty appointments, adherence to Post Discharge Visits) may include accompaniment to appointments
Complete referrals to organizations and agencies as needed
Deliver culturally appropriate health education in the areas where OSH has provided competency training to the CHW
Support care team decision making through participation in interdisciplinary team meetings
Document interactions with patients in electronic medical record in a timely manner while maintaining HIPAA standards and confidentiality of protected health information
Manage time, set priorities, work independently, and collaborate effectively with an interdisciplinary medical team
Other duties as assigned

Required

What we’re looking for

Minimum of 1 year of experience in healthcare, community-based, case management, or social service environment
Strong oral and written communication skills
Ability to manage multiple priorities while maintaining a positive attitude
Dedication to serving the community and building meaningful relationships
Proficient computer skills (i.e. Windows, GSuite, Microsoft, etc.)
Access to reliable transportation and ability to travel throughout the community to various locations
US work authorization

Strongly Preferred

Fluency in language that is commonly spoken in the community when necessary. Most often this will include Bilingual English/Spanish
Experience working on multidisciplinary teams with organizations, agencies, patients, and community members
Knowledge of community resources and resource navigation

Preferred

Community Health Worker certification or Associates or Bachelors in a related field is a plus
Experience utilizing electronic medical record systems
A problem-solving orientation and a flexible and positive attitude

40

Full time

$18.50 - $38.82

jobs.title: Senior Program Manager, Data Governance & Analytics
jobs.description:
Job Description

The Senior Program Manager, Data Governance & Analytics establishes and leads the data governance, reporting, and analytics strategy for Global Program Controls. This role is accountable for ensuring that portfolio delivery data is consistently defined, accurately maintained, appropriately governed, and translated into actionable insights for senior leadership.

As the recognized subject matter expert for program data and performance reporting, this individual will define the policies, standards, operating mechanisms, and analytical capabilities that enable trusted decision-making across the global portfolio. The role owns the authoritative delivery data framework, executive portfolio dashboards, operational reporting suite, data quality program, stewardship network, and reporting calendar.

This position operates across multiple organizations and systems, including Jira, Primavera Cloud, Apex, Unifier, financial platforms, and business intelligence tools. The Senior Program Manager will influence senior leaders, program controls teams, technology partners, finance organizations, and functional stakeholders to establish consistent data practices and improve portfolio visibility.

The successful candidate combines deep expertise in data governance, business intelligence, and program controls with strong executive communication and cross-functional leadership. This is a highly influential individual contributor role that leads enterprise-scale programs and processes through expertise, partnership, and strategic influence rather than direct people management.

Key Responsibilities

Data Governance Strategy and Leadership

Establish and lead the Global Program Controls Data Governance program, including its strategy, policies, standards, operating model, controls, and performance measures.
Develop the overarching data governance policy framework and ensure alignment with enterprise data, security, compliance, and technology requirements.
Define decision rights, ownership models, escalation paths, and governance forums for portfolio delivery data.
Advise leadership on data governance, reporting strategy, analytical capability, and portfolio performance measurement.
Evaluate emerging technologies, governance practices, and analytical approaches that can improve data quality, accessibility, automation, and decision-making.
Lead complex, cross-functional data initiatives that span multiple organizations, regions, business processes, and technology platforms.

Data Standards, Dictionary, and Lineage

Lead development and maintenance of the authoritative data dictionary for delivery data across Jira, Primavera Cloud, Unifier, financial systems, and reporting platforms.
Define standard business terms, metric definitions, calculation methodologies, source-system ownership, and acceptable-use requirements.
Establish and maintain data lineage documentation that maps data from source systems through integrations, transformations, semantic models, dashboards, and reports.
Ensure that key portfolio metrics have documented definitions, accountable owners, approved sources, and transparent calculation logic.
Resolve conflicting definitions and promote consistent use of data and metrics across teams and regions.

Data Quality and Issue Resolution

Define and enforce data quality rules for completeness, validity, accuracy, consistency, timeliness, and uniqueness.
Establish scheduled data quality monitoring, automated validation checks, exception reporting, and data quality scorecards.
Create measurable data quality targets and communicate trends, gaps, and risks to leadership and data owners.
Operate the data issue resolution process, giving stakeholders a clear mechanism to report suspected data defects.
Lead root-cause analysis and corrective-action efforts for recurring or high-impact data issues.
Partner with system owners and business teams to address upstream process weaknesses rather than relying solely on downstream corrections.
Ensure executive and operational reports are validated for accuracy and completeness before distribution.

Master Data and Data Stewardship

Govern critical master and reference data, including canonical site names, project identifiers, regional hierarchies, organizational structures, program classifications, and reporting dimensions.
Establish and manage a cross-functional data stewardship network.
Identify data owners and stewards within each functional area and define their responsibilities, decision authority, and expected service levels.
Provide training, guidance, tools, and ongoing support to data stewards and contributors.
Facilitate governance forums that address data quality, definition changes, ownership gaps, and cross-system alignment.
Mentor peers and stakeholders on governance, reporting, data interpretation, and analytical best practices.

Executive Reporting and Analytics

Own the strategy, design, development, and ongoing maintenance of the global portfolio executive dashboard and operational reporting suite.
Translate complex program, schedule, cost, risk, and workflow data into clear, visually compelling insights for vice presidents and other senior leaders.
Establish reporting standards covering templates, visualization conventions, metric definitions, validation protocols, version control, distribution, and retention.
Manage the reporting calendar and ensure reports are produced, reviewed, approved, and distributed according to established cadences.
Respond to ad hoc leadership requests for custom analysis, scenario evaluation, and portfolio deep dives.

Systems and Data Partnerships

Partner with systems integration, data engineering, IT, and application teams to ensure reliable and scalable data flows.
Define business requirements for integrations, data models, reporting layers, controls, and workflow enhancements.
Partner with system owners to align data access policies with role-based access, confidentiality, security, and business requirements.
Assess the downstream reporting and governance impact of system, process, and data-model changes.
Ensure analytical products draw from governed, traceable, and trusted data sources.
Drive adoption of reusable data products and self-service reporting capabilities while maintaining appropriate governance and controls.

Stakeholder Leadership and Influence

Build and maintain a broad network across Global Program Controls, delivery organizations, finance, IT, data engineering, system administration, and senior leadership.
Lead through influence across teams where formal authority may not exist.
Communicate recommendations, risks, tradeoffs, and decisions to both technical and non-technical audiences.
Facilitate alignment among stakeholders with competing requirements, definitions, or priorities.
Represent Global Program Controls in enterprise data, reporting, and technology forums.
Provide coaching and mentorship to analysts, program managers, data stewards, and other peers across the line of business.
Foster inclusive collaboration by ensuring relevant stakeholders are represented in governance, reporting, and decision-making activities.

Responsibilities

Required Qualifications

Extensive experience leading data governance, analytics, business intelligence, program controls, or enterprise reporting in a complex global environment.
Demonstrated experience building or significantly maturing a data governance or enterprise reporting program.
Expert knowledge of at least one relevant specialist area, such as data governance, business intelligence, program controls, data management, or portfolio analytics.
Deep understanding of:
Data quality management
Master and reference data management
Data lineage and metadata management
Data ownership and stewardship
Metric governance
Reporting controls
Analytical data modeling

Expert proficiency with Power BI or Tableau, including dashboard design, semantic or data modeling, calculated measures, and report distribution.
Strong knowledge of program controls and performance metrics, including schedule variance, cost variance, forecast accuracy, service-level performance, and earned value.
Experience extracting, interpreting, reconciling, or reporting data from Primavera P6 and Jira.
Experience defining executive dashboards and translating complex data into concise, decision-oriented narratives.
Demonstrated success influencing senior leaders and cross-functional teams across organizational boundaries.
Ability to lead multiple complex initiatives with significant business impact, ambiguity, and interdependencies.
Strong written, verbal, facilitation, and executive presentation skills.
Proficiency with Jira, Confluence, and enterprise reporting or analytics platforms.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience supporting construction, capital programs, infrastructure delivery, or data center development.
Familiarity with DAMA-DMBOK or comparable data governance frameworks.
Experience with Unifier, or similar capital project management systems.
Knowledge of financial reporting, including budget-versus-actual analysis, cash-flow forecasting, and cost forecasting.
Experience partnering with data engineering teams on integrations, transformation logic, data warehouses, or semantic reporting layers.
Experience implementing automated data quality monitoring or governance workflow tools.
Familiarity with predictive analytics, artificial intelligence, or machine-learning applications for program controls and portfolio management.
Experience operating in a large, globally distributed enterprise environment.

Key Partners

Global Program Controls leadership
Systems Integration and Data Engineering
Program and Project Controls teams
Reporting and Analytics teams
Root Cause Analysis leaders
Functional and regional pillar leads
Data owners and data stewards
Information Technology and enterprise data teams
Finance and business operations
Scheduling, cost management, risk, and delivery organizations

Scope and Impact

Serves as the recognized subject matter expert for data governance, analytics, and portfolio reporting within the line of business.
Leads strategies, programs, and operating processes that have a material impact on portfolio visibility, data trust, and leadership decision-making.
Advises senior leadership on decisions involving data strategy, performance measurement, governance, systems, and reporting.
Leads work that spans multiple functions, systems, organizations, and geographic regions.
Addresses complex and ambiguous problems by examining systemic causes, applying industry best practices, and introducing innovative or non-conventional approaches.
Regularly contributes to strategic planning and decision-making for Global Program Controls.
Establishes scalable capabilities that improve how the organization manages data, measures performance, identifies risk, and executes its global portfolio.

jobs.title: Data Analyst (HQ)
jobs.description:
Koniag Services Inc., a Koniag Government Services company, is seeking a talented and experienced Data Analyst to support headquarters-level data analysis, performance reporting, and strategic decision support for our IT Call Center program operations in the Washington, DC area. The ideal candidate is a highly analytical and detail-oriented professional with a strong command of data analytics, reporting tools, and visualization platforms, and a demonstrated ability to synthesize complex, multi-site operational data into clear and compelling insights for senior leadership and government stakeholders. They bring a strategic perspective, exceptional communication skills, and the ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced, high-visibility headquarters environment. Ability to obtain a government security clearance may be required to support Koniag Services Inc. and our government customers. This position is located in the Washington, DC area.

We offer competitive compensation and an extraordinary benefits package including health, dental and vision insurance, 401K with company matching, flexible spending accounts, paid holidays, three weeks paid time off, and more.

Position Description

The Headquarters Data Analyst will serve as a central analytical resource supporting the enterprise-wide performance monitoring, reporting, and data governance functions of the IT Call Center program. This individual will work closely with the Senior Program Manager, program leadership, and site-level operations teams to aggregate, analyze, and present program-wide performance data, support strategic planning activities, and ensure that all headquarters-level reporting requirements are met with accuracy and consistency. Principal responsibilities will include but are not limited to:

Serve as the primary data analyst supporting headquarters-level program performance monitoring, aggregating and analyzing operational data from multiple call center sites to provide a comprehensive, enterprise-wide view of program performance.

About Our Client
The organization operates in the field of pediatric infectious disease research, focusing on improving treatment outcomes for children with tuberculosis (TB). It addresses challenges in pediatric TB care by conducting clinical trials and research studies designed to identify shorter, safer, and more effective treatment regimens. Its research programs involve collaboration across international clinical sites, expanding the reach and impact of its work.
About the Opportunity
The Research Data Analyst
supports data analysis and clinical research activities for studies including the SMART4TB TA2 Therapeutics study and the SMILE-TB trial. This role contributes to data collection, statistical analysis, reporting, and database management while applying clinical expertise to interpret pediatric TB research findings. The position also supports data quality, participant safety, and collaboration across multidisciplinary research teams.

• Collect research data and generate reports, analytical models, and study findings.
• Run statistical models and prepare analytical reports for assigned research studies.

• Design tables and other formats to clearly present analytical results.
• Manage or assist with data entry and maintenance of research databases.
• Review, edit, and finalize study-related documents in collaboration with research teams.
• Review and summarize safety data, including adverse event reports.
• Provide clinical guidance regarding the management and interpretation of pediatric TB adverse events.
• Participate as a clinical expert in the Clinical Management Committee.
• Support data analysis teams by providing clinical interpretation of research findings.
• Generate, review, and resolve data queries within REDCap.

• Collaborate with investigators, data management teams, and clinical research personnel as needed.
• Perform additional research and analytical duties as assigned.

• Bachelor’s degree in a relevant discipline.

new_jobs.title: Petco Love - Data Analyst
new_jobs.description:
Want to help pets live their best lives?

We’re proud to be where the pets go and where the pet people go. If you want to make a real difference, create an exciting career path, feel welcome to be your whole self and nurture your wellbeing, Petco is the place for you
.

Our core values capture that spirit as we work to improve lives by doing what’s right for pets and people.

Pet First – Protect & Empower. All pets should Live their Best Life. We put the needs of pets and pet parents at the center of everything we do.
Foster the Fun – Connect & Bond. Our Passion for pets brings us together! We celebrate the journey of pet parenthood through district experiences, products, and services.
Let’s Go! Own & Commit. We are stronger as One Petco team. We bring our unique superpowers and champion authenticity in everyone to drive success.

About Petco

We’re proud to be "where the pets go"
to find everything they need to live their best lives for more than 60 years — from their favorite meals and toys, to trusted supplies and expert support from people who get it, because we live it. We believe in the universal truths of pet parenthood — the boundless boops, missing slippers, late night zoomies and everything in between. And we’re here for it. Every tail wag, every vet visit, every step of the way. We are 29,000+
strong and together we nurture the pet-human bond in more than 1,500
Petco stores across the U.S., Mexico and Puerto Rico, 250+
Vetco Total Care hospitals, hundreds of preventive care clinics and eight distribution centers. In 1999, we founded Petco Love. Together, we support thousands of local animal welfare groups nationwide and have helped find homes for approximately 7 million animals
through in-store adoption events.

About Petco Love

Petco Love is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit on a mission to create a future where no pet is ever lost, separated, or without a loving home. Our flagship platform, Petco Love Lost, is an AI/ML-powered national lost and found pet search tool that has facilitated over 120,000 reunions annually, covers 90% of U.S. animal shelters, and serves millions of pet parents across the country.

We operate at the intersection of technology, animal welfare, and community impact. Our small, mission-driven team moves fast, works closely with partners across the shelter and rescue ecosystem, and builds products that matter.

The Role

We are looking for a Data Analyst to join Petco Love's product and marketing team. This is a hands-on role with high visibility across our platform, GTM initiatives, and partner integrations. You will own our analytics infrastructure end-to-end, from raw event tracking in GA4 through BigQuery to dashboards and decision-ready insights that directly inform product and marketing strategy.

You will work closely with the Chief Product Officer, CTO, and Customer Success team. You do not need to be a data scientist, but you need to be deeply curious, self-directed, and excited about using data to drive mission impact.

Essential Job Functions

Analytics & Data Infrastructure

Own and maintain our GA4 implementation, including event schema design, custom dimensions, conversion tracking, and data layer governance across petcolovelost.org and related product surfaces.
Build and manage our GA4 to BigQuery pipeline as our primary analytics data warehouse; design schemas, write transformation queries, and maintain data quality standards.
Develop and maintain dashboards and reports that track product performance, user behavior, funnel conversion, and mission KPIs (reunions, sign-ups, NPS, shelter engagement).
Apply advanced analytical techniques including behavioral segmentation, funnel analysis, predictive modeling, and cohort analysis to surface insights across the pet owner and shelter user journey.
Mine large datasets to identify patterns in user behavior, feature engagement, search performance, and platform outcomes to inform product roadmap and marketing decisions.

GTM Strategy & Marketing Analytics

Partner with the product and marketing team to design and analyze GTM experiments including A/B tests, flow variants, and audience segmentation strategies across email, SMS, and in-product channels.
Build and maintain audience models and signal-based segmentation to power our product and marketing automation architecture, including found-pet, lost-pet, and partner-specific flows.
Provide data support for partnership GTM initiatives including revenue modeling, audience sizing, and performance tracking.
Translate campaign and flow performance data (open rates, click rates, conversions, reunion outcomes) into clear recommendations that optimize acquisition, engagement, and lifetime value.
Build accurate financial projections and impact forecasts based on deep behavioral analysis to support board reporting, partner proposals, and strategic planning.

Animal Welfare & Mission Insights

Apply understanding of animal welfare industry dynamics to contextualize data findings and surface insights specific to shelter intake, outcomes, lost and found behavior, and pet owner decision-making.
Analyze survey and behavioral research data to identify unmet needs and product opportunities.
Validate AI/ML model outputs and surface quality signals from our facial recognition matching and pet identity systems to help the engineering team maintain accuracy and reduce false positives.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

Collaborate with Customer Success to identify trends in user-reported issues, NPS driver analysis, and segment-level satisfaction signals.
Present findings to senior leadership and board stakeholders; translate complex analysis into clear narrative, actionable recommendations, and visual summaries that drive decisions.
Contribute to long-term projects from scoping through execution, partnering with engineering, design, and external platform teams (shelters, rescue partners, plaform integrations).

Required Skills And Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in economics, statistics, math, computer science, or related field; Master's preferred.
1-2+ years of experience in a data analytics or quantitative role.
Hands-on experience with GA4 — event tracking, custom dimensions, exploration reports, and integration with BigQuery (Google Analytics 4 to BigQuery export).
Strong SQL skills; experience querying large, complex datasets across multiple sources.
Experience with statistical programming languages (Python preferred; R or SAS acceptable).
Demonstrated ability to build clear, decision-oriented dashboards and visualizations (Looker, Tableau, Google Data Studio, or similar).
Exceptional communication skills — ability to translate complex data into plain, compelling narratives for non-technical stakeholders including executives and board members.
Ability to prioritize and manage multiple workstreams simultaneously in a fast-moving environment.
Genuine intellectual curiosity and commitment to solving hard problems with limited resources.

Nice to Have

Experience with Klaviyo or similar marketing automation platforms — audience segmentation, flow analytics, or A/B testing.
Familiarity with animal welfare, pet tech, nonprofit, or mission-driven organizations.
Experience with AI/ML data validation or working alongside data science teams on model quality.
Knowledge of the shelter/rescue ecosystem, pet reunification, or pet adoption platforms.

new_jobs.title: Clinical Program Manager
new_jobs.description:
At Gilead, we’re creating a healthier world for all people. For more than 35 years, we’ve tackled diseases such as HIV, viral hepatitis, COVID-19 and cancer – working relentlessly to develop therapies that help improve lives and to ensure access to these therapies across the globe. We continue to fight against the world’s biggest health challenges, and our mission requires collaboration, determination and a relentless drive to make a difference.

Every member of Gilead’s team plays a critical role in the discovery and development of life-changing scientific innovations. Our employees are our greatest asset as we work to achieve our bold ambitions, and we’re looking for the next wave of passionate and ambitious people ready to make a direct impact.

We believe every employee deserves a great leader. People Leaders are the cornerstone to the employee experience at Gilead and Kite. As a people leader now or in the future, you are the key driver in evolving our culture and creating an environment where every employee feels included, developed and empowered to fulfil their aspirations. Join Gilead and help create possible, together.

Job Description

The Clinical Program Manager
is responsible for the worldwide execution of all Phase I - IV clinical trials across all Gilead therapeutic areas. Clinical Operations plays a key role in ensuring all Gilead clinical trials are performed in accordance with applicable SOPs, company policies and regulatory guidelines to provide timely and high-quality clinical data that supports global registration and commercialization of Gilead’s products.

You will oversee and be responsible for the successful execution of studies and/or multiple studies within a program or multiple programs, including financial responsibility. You will be responsible for the resource management of studies, including ongoing assessment of resource needs and optimal deployment of resources to support a fluid ‘One Ops’ workforce.

You will participate and engage in Clinical Operations and/or cross-functional organizational change initiatives. You may act as the business process owner (BPO) and/or serve as a subject matter expert for Clinical Operations processes. You will encourage an innovative mindset by championing new ideas and initiatives and incorporating best practices, external benchmarking, and standardization across Clinical Operations.

This is a Hybrid position, 3 days on-site (Tues -Thurs). Will not consider fully remote candidates.

Job Responsibilities

Provides ongoing financial oversight of clinical trials/programs assigned.
May provide input into strategic and operational short- and long-range therapeutic area / functional area plans as appropriate, including supporting alignment and communications to other team members upon implementation.
Provides guidance and oversight for the successful management of all aspects of clinical trials within designated program budgets and timelines.
Leads cross-functional Study Management Teams (SMTs) and influences all relevant stakeholders.
Partners with cross-functional teams to manage, adjust and revise project timelines and budgets as needed.
Communicates project status and issues and ensures project team goals are met in alignment with project decisions. Escalates issues as needed.
Participates in the development of all study-related documentation, including study protocols.
Participates in the selection, management and oversight of contract research organizations (CROs) / vendors, including development of requests for proposals (RFPs).
Anticipates obstacles and difficulties and implements solutions to achieve project goals, including risk assessment and mitigation strategies.
Resolves issues as needed within national and international regulations and guidelines.
Uses all available tools to track, oversee and communicate on program status to all key stakeholders.
Participates in and/or leads departmental or interdepartmental strategic initiatives.
As assigned, initiates, authors, or otherwise contributes to standard operating procedure (SOP) development, implementation, and training.
Responsible for Clinical Operations activities conducted by the affiliate that are required by local regulations and/or usual practice to support clinical trials.
Ensures team’s work complies with established practices, policies and processes, and any regulatory or other requirements.
People Leader Path: Hires, develops, and retains diverse top talent on the team. Sets clear expectations for direct reports, and coaches direct reports on their performance, development and career interests.

Basic Requirements

BA / BS / RN with 8 or more years’ relevant clinical or related experience in life sciences or MA / MS / PharmD / PhD with 6 or more years’ relevant clinical or related experience in life sciences.
Minimum of 4 years’ cross-functional study management or related leadership experience in life sciences, including multiple years’ experience managing study or project teams.
Experience developing RFPs and selection and oversight/management of CROs or other vendors.
Proven ability to successfully start-up, manage and close-out clinical studies, including authoring clinical study and regulatory documentation and SOPs.

Preferred Requirements

Advanced knowledge of one or more disease or therapeutic areas, as evidenced by independence in designing, implementing, and managing study team plans, deliverables and resource management.
Complete knowledge of full cycle study management, from start-up to close-out.
Advanced knowledge of study management best practices and tools and has shown ability to apply these to improve study efficiencies and effectiveness.
Thorough knowledge of Food & Drug Administration (FDA) and European Medicines Agency (EMA), and other applicable national regulations, International Council for Harmonisation of Technical Requirements for Pharmaceuticals for Human Use (ICH) guidelines and Good Clinical Practice (GCP) governing the conduct of clinical studies.
Proven ability to effectively author clinical study and regulatory documentation.
Ability to lead and influence programs, projects and/or initiatives.
Strong interpersonal skills and understanding of team dynamics.
Proven ability to work successfully in a team-oriented, highly matrixed environment.
Demonstrated effectiveness coaching, guiding and directing the work of others, effectively managing performance of others, and developing team capabilities.
Demonstrated effectiveness in proactively managing change.
Strong communication and organizational skills.
As required, the ability to travel

People Leader Accountabilities

Create Inclusion - knowing the business value of diverse teams, modeling inclusion, and embedding the value of diversity in the way they manage their teams.
Develop Talent - understand the skills, experience, aspirations and potential of their employees and coach them on current performance and future potential. They ensure employees are receiving the feedback and insight needed to grow, develop and realize their purpose.
Empower Teams - connect the team to the organization by aligning goals, purpose, and organizational objectives, and holding them to account. They provide the support needed to remove barriers and connect their team to the broader ecosystem.

The Salary Range For This Position Is

Bay Area: $182,070.00 - $235,620.00.

Other US Locations: $165,495.00 - $214,170.00.

new_jobs.title: Care Manager II - Case Management
new_jobs.description:
Description

Summary:

The Care Manager (CM) II works in collaboration with the patient/family, physicians and multidisciplinary team members to ensure patient progression through the continuum of care and to develop a plan of care for each assigned patient from admission through discharge. The CM is responsible for identifying, initiating and managing optimal patient flow/throughput to enhance continuity of care, smooth and safe transitions, patient satisfaction, patient safety, and length of stay management. Support and expertise are provided through comprehensive assessment, planning, implementation, and overall evaluation of individual patient needs. Care Coordination and Discharge Planning are both responsibilities of this role. The CM assesses and responds to patient/family needs by coordinating efforts of other team members and identifies and resolves barriers that hinder effective patient care. The CM adheres to departmental and organizational goals, objectives, standards of performance, policies and procedures, and continually assures regulatory compliance.

Responsibilities

Meets expectations of the applicable OneCHRISTUS Competencies: Leader of Self, Leader of Others, or Leader of Leaders.
Coordinates the integration of case management functions into the patient care and discharge planning processes in collaboration with other hospital departments, external service organizations, agencies, and healthcare facilities.
Coordinates/facilitates patient care progression throughout the continuum of care in an efficient and cost-effective manner.
Serves as resource, provides support, and advocates on behalf of the patient related to treatment decisions and end of life issues.
Closely monitor patient length of stay in regard to the geometric mean length of stay and communicate/collaborate with appropriate interdisciplinary team members to remove barriers and expedite discharge.
Implements and monitors the patient’s plan of care to ensure effectiveness and appropriateness of services.
Identifies and escalates local and system barriers that are impeding diagnostic or treatment progress and issues related to quality and risk as appropriate in a timely manner.
Proactively identifies and resolves delays and obstacles to discharge.
Uses advanced conflict resolution skills as necessary to ensure timely resolution of issues.
Collaborates with medical staff, nursing staff, and ancillary staff to eliminate barriers to efficient delivery of care in the appropriate setting.
Interviews patients/families to obtain information about social, emotional, and financial factors which impact health status to develop comprehensive discharge planning assessment and care plan.
Assesses needs for discharge planning and continuing care/resource support following discharge; independently makes recommendations to patients and families regarding post-acute level of care needs and options including:
Acute Rehabilitation Placement
Nursing Home or Skilled Nursing placement
Psychiatric or Substance Abuse placement
New Dialysis
Child/Adult/Domestic Abuse
Home Health/Hospice Referrals
Legal issues (adoptions, guardianship)
Assistance with Advance Directives
Community Resource needs
Financial Issues/Funding options
DME Referrals and Coordination
Social Determinants of Health

Initiates discharge planning at the time of admission and makes post-hospital service referrals based upon information gathered during assessment and interactions with physicians, multidisciplinary care team, and payors as indicated.
Acts as patient advocate by negotiating for, and coordinating, resources with payors, agencies, and vendors.
Ensures that all elements critical to the plan of care have been communicated to the patient/family and members of the healthcare team and are documented as necessary to assure continuity of care.
Provide appropriate interventions which demonstrate knowledge of and sensitivity toward cultural diversity and the religious, developmental, health literacy, and educational backgrounds of the patient population.
Assesses the patient’s formal and informal support system as well as available benefits and/or community resources.
Meets directly with patient/family to assess needs and develop and individualized care plan in collaboration with the physician.
Ensures and maintains plan consensus from patient/family, physician and payor.
Provides education, information, direction, and support related to patient’s goals of care.
Acts as patient advocate to develop treatment plan and coordinate patient care and to transition patient to the appropriate next level of care.
Demonstrates and promotes respect for the dignity and rights of every patient while adhering to the safety standards and practices of the organization and the nursing profession.
Collaborates with the physician and other health care professionals to promote appropriate use of medical center resources.
Provides information and support to patients and families, helping them access needed resources within the medical center and community.
Actively participates in clinical performance improvement activities involving length of stay, resource utilization, avoidable days, cost per case, and readmissions.
Measures effectiveness of interventions through direct communication with post-acute care providers, patients, and caregivers.
Promotes individual professional growth and development by meeting requirements for mandatory/continuing education and skills competency.
Actively participates in Multidisciplinary/Patient Care Progression Rounds.
Escalates cases as appropriate and per policy to Physician Advisors and/or CM Director.
Documents in the medical record per regulatory and department guidelines.
May be asked to assist with special projects.
May serve a preceptor or orienter to new associates.
Assumes responsibility for professional growth and development.
Must have excellent verbal and written communication and ability to interact with diverse populations.
Must have critical and analytical thinking skills.
Must have demonstrated clinical competency.
Must have the ability to Multitask and to function in a stressful and fast paced environment.
Must have working knowledge of discharge planning, utilization management, case management, performance improvement, and managed care reimbursement.
Must have understanding of pre-acute and post-acute levels of care and community resources.
Must have ability to work independently and exercise sound judgment in interactions with physicians, payors, patients and their families.
Must be understanding of internal and external resources and knowledge of available community resources.

We’re building a world of health around every individual — shaping a more connected, convenient and compassionate health experience. Join us and be part of something bigger – helping to simplify health care one person, one family and one community at a time.

Title:

Company:
Oak Street Health

Role Description

The purpose of a Community Health Worker (CHW) at Oak Street Health is to act as the bridge between our patients, community, and medical systems in order to remove barriers and increase wellness across all life domains. A CHW is a patient’s advocate or liaison, accompanying patients through proactive in-person and phone outreach based on their care needs to promote health literacy and increase access to resources needed to live healthier lives. High levels of flexibility, problem solving, strong communication, and an intimate knowledge of the community served are required to be successful.

CHWs work closely with Medical Social Workers to manage patient care plans, support care team decision making, and coordinate clinical and complementary services needed to provide high quality health care and improve the quality and cultural competence of service delivery. CHWs are expected to work within their scope of practice. There is no expected clinical license for this position.

Core Responsibilities

Establish and maintain strong interpersonal relationships with patients, community organizations, team members, and partners to coordinate patient needs
Manage patient referrals defined by the care team & collaborate with the Medical Social Worker on action plan
Facilitate communication between all identified parties involved in patients’ care as needed (e.g., family members, caregivers, medical providers, community-based organizations)
Form relationships with and build an inventory of local community organizations that may benefit our patients
Connect patients to state and local community resources related to housing, transportation, food, and activities of daily living among other social and physical barriers to health.
Assist patients with completion of applications for accessing eligible benefits and resources
Promote goal setting and achievement to improve patients’ quality of life and self efficacy with patients. Goal definitions are agreed upon by the care team
Meet with patients in patient-centered and patient-preferred locations (e.g., Oak Street Health center, patient’s home, external medical provider facility, community setting)
Community Health Workers should plan to spend about half of their time outside of the center in patient-centered locations; this means having access to a reliable means of transportation to do so is required
Drive engagement with high risk individuals (e.g., completed specialty appointments, adherence to Post Discharge Visits) may include accompaniment to appointments
Complete referrals to organizations and agencies as needed
Deliver culturally appropriate health education in the areas where OSH has provided competency training to the CHW
Support care team decision making through participation in interdisciplinary team meetings
Document interactions with patients in electronic medical record in a timely manner while maintaining HIPAA standards and confidentiality of protected health information
Manage time, set priorities, work independently, and collaborate effectively with an interdisciplinary medical team

The Care Manager (CM) III works in collaboration with the patient/family, physicians, and multidisciplinary team members to ensure patient progression through the continuum of care and to develop a plan of care for each assigned patient from admission through discharge. The CM is responsible for identifying, initiating, and managing optimal patient flow/throughput to enhance continuity of care, smooth and safe transitions, patient satisfaction, patient safety, and length of stay management. Support and expertise are provided through comprehensive assessment, planning, implementation, and overall evaluation of individual patient needs. Care Coordination and Discharge Planning are both responsibilities of this role. The CM assesses and responds to patient/family needs by coordinating the efforts of other team members and identifies and resolves barriers that hinder effective patient care. The CM adheres to departmental and organizational goals, objectives, standards of performance, policies, and procedures, and continually assures regulatory compliance.

Responsibilities

Meets expectations of the applicable OneCHRISTUS Competencies: Leader of Self, Leader of Others, or Leader of Leaders.
Coordinates the integration of case management functions into the patient care and discharge planning processes in collaboration with other hospital departments, external service organizations, agencies, and healthcare facilities.
Coordinates/facilitates patient care progression throughout the continuum of care in an efficient and cost-effective manner.
Serves as a resource and provides support related to treatment decisions and end-of-life issues.
Closely monitor the patient's length of stay in regard to the geometric mean length of stay and communicate/collaborate with appropriate interdisciplinary team members to remove barriers and expedite discharge.
Implements and monitors the patient’s plan of care to ensure effectiveness and appropriateness of services.
Identifies and escalates local and system barriers that are impeding diagnostic or treatment progress and issues related to quality and risk as appropriate in a timely manner.
Proactively identifies and resolves delays and obstacles to discharge.
Uses advanced conflict resolution skills as necessary to ensure timely resolution of issues.
Collaborates with medical staff, nursing staff, and ancillary staff to eliminate barriers to efficient delivery of care in the appropriate setting.
Interview patients/families to obtain information about social, emotional, and financial factors that impact health status to develop a comprehensive discharge planning assessment and care plan.
Assesses needs for discharge planning and continuing care/resource support following discharge; independently makes recommendations to patients and families regarding the post-acute level of care needs and options including:
Acute Rehabilitation Placement

Psychiatric or Substance Abuse placement
New Dialysis
Child/Adult/Domestic Abuse

Legal issues (adoptions, guardianship)

Community Resource needs
Financial Issues/Funding options
DME Referrals and Coordination

Ensures that all elements critical to the plan of care have been communicated to the patient/family and members of the healthcare team and are documented as necessary to assure continuity of care.
Provide appropriate interventions which demonstrate knowledge of and sensitivity toward cultural diversity and the religious, developmental, health literacy, and educational backgrounds of the patient population.
Assesses the patient’s formal and informal support system as well as available benefits and/or community resources.

Demonstrates and promotes respect for the dignity and rights of every patient while adhering to the safety standards and practices of the organization and the nursing profession.
Collaborates with the physician and other health care professionals to promote appropriate use of medical center resources.
Provides information and support to patients and families, helping them access needed resources within the medical center and community.
Actively participates in clinical performance improvement activities involving length of stay, resource utilization, avoidable days, cost per case, and readmissions.
